To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the insertion of the extra‐domain B of fibronectins renders accessible a novel cryptic sequence that is recognized by a high affinity monoclonal antibody that targets tumors.

a novel human fibronactin cryptic sequence is unmasked by insertion of the angiogenetic associated extra type III domain and that the corresponding epitope represents an additional angiogenesis‐related target.
a novel human fibronactin cryptic sequence is unmasked by insertion of the angiogenetic‐associated extra type 3 domain B.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of new angiogenesis targets, the development of new diagnostic tools and the study of the biological role of the novel cryptic epitopes.
the identification of novel targets for cancer therapy, and the generation of new diagnostic tools.
the development of new molecular tools for the study and the diagnosis of angiogenesis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the insertion of the B‐domain into the FN molecule is responsible for the appearance of the C6 epitope, which is a novel cryptic sequence in the type III repeat 10 of the FN molecule, and that the B‐domain is not responsible for the binding to the C6 antibody.
the insertion of the ED‐B in FN is not a simple event of alternative splicing, but it is a process that involves the unmasking of a novel FN sequence that may have an important biological role.

this study demonstrates that the C6 antibody is a useful tool in the study of the biological function of the cryptic sequence in FN, and that this cryptic sequence could be a potential target for the treatment of tumors.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a cryptic sequence in the FN molecule, that is normally masked by the presence of the EDB, can be revealed by the insertion of EDB.

we have identified a new cryptic sequence of fibronectins that is unmasked in the presence of the EDB, a sequence that we have used to generate a new anti‐fibronectin antibody, which is useful for tumor targeting and for the study of tumor angiogenesis.
we have identified a cryptic sequence in fibronectin that becomes available for interaction with other molecules when the EDB is inserted.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a novel cryptic epitope of FN is unmasked by EDB insertion.
the insertion of the extra type III repeat B in the fibronectin molecule unmasked a novel cryptic sequence that is specifically recognized by a monoclonal antibody.
we have identified a novel cryptic epitope of fibronectins that is exposed only when the angiogenic isoforms are expressed.
